arch_decisions.decision: Effective-state helper: timestamp-driven lazy activation (D4). Add nullable scheduled_start_at / scheduled_end_at columns to app.examinations and introduce ONE authoritative helper, ExaminationEffectiveState(exam) -> {phase: 'inactive'|'active'|'ended', activeNow bool}, consulted by the activation gate, the submission gate, the questions gate, and the SSE push. effective active = is_active=true AND (scheduled_start_at IS NULL OR now()>=scheduled_start_at) AND (scheduled_end_at IS NULL OR now()<scheduled_end_at). 'Instant activate' = set is_active=true, activated_at=now(), scheduled_start_at=now(), scheduled_end_at=NULL. 'Activate at time, limited window' = is_active=true, scheduled_start_at=T0, scheduled_end_at=T1 (sandbox NOT cloned yet). 'Deactivate at time' = set scheduled_end_at=T1 (the lazy gate stops accepting submissions at T1 even though is_active stays true until a real deactivate drops the sandbox). 'Instant deactivate' = existing Phase 3 ArchiveExamination (is_active=false, archived_at=now(), drop sandbox). Lazy sandbox prep: on the FIRST request inside the active window that needs the sandbox (first DML submission OR first GetExamQuestions that detects examHasDMLQuestions), call InitializeExamSandbox(examID) guarded by app.exam_sandboxes (created_at IS NOT NULL, dropped_at IS NULL) so it clones at most once; InitializeExamSandbox is already idempotent. The activation PRE-FLIGHT (every question expected_result_status='captured') still runs at the moment is_active is flipped to true, regardless of scheduled_start_at, so a scheduled exam cannot be armed with uncaptured questions.
arch_decisions.rationale: D4 mandates no background scheduler/cron. A single pure helper computing effective state from now() vs timestamps at request time keeps all four gates consistent and avoids split-brain between a boolean and a clock. Reusing is_active as the 'armed' flag and scheduled_* as the window keeps the existing freeze logic (UpsertQuestion/ImportSchema/AssignStudents check is_active) working unchanged. Lazy sandbox prep honors the constraint that pure-SELECT exams never clone and that DML exams must have a sandbox ready on first access, without a scheduler.

arch_decisions.decision: SSE realtime activation push (D2, R10) — the infrastructure R9 depends on. Add a new authenticated SSE endpoint GET /api/v1/quiz/exams/:id/stream that holds an HTTP connection open and pushes a single 'exam-status' event whenever the exam's effective state (ARCH-001) transitions to active for an enrolled student. Server model: an in-process pub/sub hub (services/sse_hub.go) keyed by examID, holding a set of subscriber channels. gin handler: authenticate (see token note), verify enrollment, set headers (Content-Type: text/event-stream, Cache-Control: no-cache, Connection: keep-alive, X-Accel-Buffering: no), register a buffered channel with the hub, then loop with c.Stream / Flush emitting: (a) an immediate snapshot event computed from ExaminationEffectiveState so a client connecting AFTER activation is told 'active' at once (no race), (b) periodic ':keepalive' comments every ~20s to defeat idle proxies, (c) the 'start' event when the hub broadcasts activation. Each event carries id: <unix-ms> for Last-Event-ID. Activation trigger: ActivateExamination (instant) and the lazy gate that first observes now()>=scheduled_start_at both call hub.Broadcast(examID, statusEvent). Because scheduled activation has no background tick, the snapshot-on-connect plus a client-side fallback poll (ARCH-009) covers the gap where the window opens while a student waits with an already-open stream — the lazy trigger fires on the first enrolled student's poll/stream-reconnect, which then broadcasts to all held connections. Reconnection: EventSource auto-reconnects; server reads Last-Event-ID but state is idempotent (re-sends current snapshot), so no event log is needed. Graceful shutdown: hub closes all channels on SIGTERM (tolerant-of-restarts per constraints; clients auto-reconnect).
arch_decisions.rationale: D2 locks SSE. SSE removes polling for a one-way server->client 'start' signal, needs no extra infra (no Redis/Kafka), and a single Go process trivially holds 90-150 idle held connections (goroutine + channel each). WebSocket REJECTED: bidirectional, needs Upgrade handshake + nginx proxy upgrade plumbing the current config explicitly strips, and we only need one-way push. Nginx LB REJECTED: only spreads polling load, never removes the poll; SSE eliminates it. Snapshot-on-connect eliminates the activation/connection race that a naive broadcast-only design would have.

arch_decisions.decision: SSE client fallback poll + Nginx SSE passthrough (supports ARCH-002/003). The frontend useExamStream composable also runs a low-frequency fallback poll (e.g. every 15s) of GET /quiz/exams?include_inactive=true (or a lightweight GET /quiz/exams/:id status) ONLY while in WAITING state, so that: (a) if the SSE connection fails behind a hostile proxy the student still transitions, and (b) for a SCHEDULED window with no background tick, the first enrolled student's poll crossing scheduled_start_at fires the lazy activation trigger which broadcasts to all held SSE connections. Nginx gains a dedicated location ~ ^/api/v1/quiz/exams/[0-9]+/stream block with proxy_buffering off, proxy_cache off, proxy_read_timeout 3600s, chunked_transfer_encoding off, and the same proxy_pass to backend:8080. The general /api/ block is unchanged.
arch_decisions.rationale: SSE through Nginx requires proxy_buffering off and a long read timeout or the stream is buffered/closed. The fallback poll is the safety net D2's held-connection model needs given D4's no-scheduler constraint: someone has to cross the timestamp boundary, and the waiting students polling at 15s is the trigger source. Bounded worst-case waiting latency = poll interval.

NO course/owner scoping column: at 5-10 categories per course on a single-course-at-a-time deployment, a flat global namespace is sufficient and a course_id FK would be speculative future-proofing with no table to reference (there is no courses entity today). schema_name naming convention is the deterministic 'practice_cat_<id>' computed AFTER insert (SERIAL id is known only post-insert), so creation is a two-step within one tx: INSERT RETURNING id, then UPDATE schema_name='practice_cat_'||id, then CREATE SCHEMA practice_cat_<id>. Provide a package-level helper PracticeCategorySchemaName(categoryID int) string returning fmt.Sprintf("practice_cat_%d", categoryID), mirroring the existing ExamSandboxName(examID) convention (postgres.go:404). The owned schema is created empty (no table clone) at category-create time; population is a separate explicit import step (ARCH-014) so a brand-new category with no curriculum loaded is a valid, query-less state.
arch_decisions.rationale: Decision 1 (user-locked): category = first-class entity owning its own schema. Reusing the SERIAL-id-then-derive-schema-name pattern matches ExamSandboxName and avoids a name-collision class. No course scoping because no courses entity exists and scale is tiny (user decision 3); adding it now is the over-engineering the brief warns against. Empty-on-create keeps category creation cheap and decouples it from the heavier import step, so the lecturer can create the category, then load its database when ready.

arch_decisions.decision: practice_questions.category (free-text) -> category_id FK migration, with data backfill. Add column app.practice_questions.category_id INTEGER REFERENCES app.practice_categories(id). category_id is NOT NULL after backfill, enforced as the final migration step. One-time idempotent data migration inside InitializeSystemTables (runs after both tables exist): (1) for every DISTINCT non-null app.practice_questions.category string that has no matching app.practice_categories.name, INSERT a category row (name=the string, created_by = the practice question's created_by or a fallback admin id, schema_name placeholder then derived) and CREATE its 'practice_cat_<id>' schema; (2) UPDATE app.practice_questions SET category_id = (SELECT id FROM app.practice_categories WHERE name = practice_questions.category) WHERE category_id IS NULL; (3) ensure an 'Uncategorized' category exists and backfill any still-null category_id to it (covers empty-string/edge rows); (4) only after all rows have category_id, run ALTER TABLE app.practice_questions ALTER COLUMN category_id SET NOT NULL. The legacy free-text 'category' TEXT column is KEPT physically for one release (not dropped) to allow rollback and to avoid breaking any in-flight reads; it becomes write-dead (new writes ignore it). A follow-up cleanup TODO may DROP COLUMN category later. All migration statements must be idempotent/re-runnable (guard inserts with NOT EXISTS / ON CONFLICT (name) DO NOTHING; guard the SET NOT NULL with a check that no NULLs remain, or wrap so a re-run is a no-op).
arch_decisions.rationale: Decision 5 (user-locked): replace free-text category with category_id FK, migrate existing values by creating one category per distinct string and backfilling. NOT NULL is correct because every practice question must live in exactly one category (a category owns the schema the question runs against - a null category_id would have no schema to execute in). 'Uncategorized' is the safety net for malformed/empty legacy values. Keeping the old TEXT column for one release de-risks the migration (the brief warns against silent data loss) and matches the project's idempotent-in-InitializeSystemTables migration convention (ARCHITECTURE.md Schema Migrations).

arch_decisions.decision: Generalize schema import to target an arbitrary schema (category-scoped import). Today ExecuteSchemaScript (postgres.go:311) runs a raw .sql against the connection with no schema qualification - it lands in whatever search_path resolves (public). Introduce a schema-targeted import used by categories WITHOUT disturbing the existing public import. Add repo method ImportSchemaIntoCategory(ctx, categoryID int, sql string, importedBy int) error that: (1) resolves the category -> its schema_name (practice_cat_<id>); (2) runs the script with the category schema first on the search_path so unqualified CREATE TABLE / INSERT land in the category schema, via a transaction doing 'SET LOCAL search_path TO <category_schema>, public' then Exec(sql) (mirrors evaluateDML's SET LOCAL search_path pattern, postgres.go:1544); (3) is NOT gated by the exam-active freeze (the category schema is independent of public and the exam source - this is the whole point of the separation, see ARCH-015); (4) optionally records an audit row reusing app.schema_import_audit with an added nullable category_id column, or a sibling table - implementor's choice, audit is secondary. The existing ExecuteSchemaScript(public) path and its exam-active freeze stay UNCHANGED for the curriculum/exam import. Rationale for not refactoring ExecuteSchemaScript's signature in place: the public import MUST keep its freeze and its audit; the category import MUST NOT freeze and is schema-scoped - different policy, so a separate method is clearer than a polymorphic flag. NOTE: a raw .sql authored as 'CREATE TABLE public.foo' (schema-qualified) would bypass the search_path redirect; document that category import scripts must use unqualified names, OR strip/reject explicit 'public.' / cross-schema qualifiers (open question OQ-2).
arch_decisions.rationale: Decision 3 (user): reuse/generalize ImportSchema to target the category schema; specify the signature change. Using SET LOCAL search_path to redirect unqualified DDL is the minimal, lowest-risk generalization and reuses the exact pattern already proven in evaluateDML. A separate method (rather than mutating ExecuteSchemaScript) preserves the public path's freeze+audit policy untouched, honoring 'exam path unchanged' and avoiding a regression in the hardened admin import surface (ARCH-010).

arch_decisions.decision: Practice stays LIVE during active exams (lift the freeze for practice). Because each practice category now owns a SEPARATE schema (practice_cat_<id>) that is NOT cloned from and NOT shared with the exam source (public / sandbox_exam_<id>), the original reason for ExamFreezeMiddleware on practice - split-brain over the shared public/sandbox_practice template - no longer applies to category-backed practice. DECISION: remove ExamFreezeMiddleware from the practice student route group (cmd/main.go:180) so students may practice while an exam is active. Safety analysis: (a) Exam SELECT submissions read public under exam_student_readonly; practice category schemas are distinct schemas, so concurrent practice SELECT/DML touches different physical tables - no row contention with the exam. (b) The exam 'public is frozen' invariant (ExecuteSchemaScript refuses while active) is about the lecturer not re-importing the curriculum mid-exam; practice category imports target practice_cat_* schemas and are correctly NOT frozen (ARCH-014). (c) Shared role/connection-pool: practice and exam both use the exam_student/exam_student_readonly roles and the same pgxpool; this is already true today and is fine - roles gate privileges, not isolation, and each submission is its own tx with SET LOCAL search_path. (d) DDL-lock concern: a category import (CREATE TABLE in practice_cat_*) takes locks only within that schema and cannot block exam queries on public. (e) The global in-process FIFO submission queue / advisory-lock partitioning (FNV1a 'practice:'+table vs exam namespace, ARCHITECTURE.md) already isolates practice from exam serialization. CONCLUSION: lifting the freeze achieves the user's separation goal with no identified contention. The ExamFreezeMiddleware code itself is retained (still used conceptually for any future shared-resource path) but is unwired from the practice group; alternatively delete its use entirely - implementor removes it from the practiceStudent group only.
arch_decisions.rationale: Decision item 5 of the brief explicitly asks for this judgment and states LIVE is preferred because it achieves the separation goal. The per-category-schema design removes the shared-state coupling that justified the freeze. Each submission is a self-contained tx with SET LOCAL search_path + SAVEPOINT/ROLLBACK, so there is no cross-schema mutation. Keeping practice live during exams is the entire user-visible payoff of separating the databases.

arch_decisions.decision: Practice submission/preview execution rewrite: resolve question -> category -> category schema; run there with SAVEPOINT/ROLLBACK (DML) and search_path-scoped SELECT (QUERY). Replace the two hardcoded 'sandbox_practice' literals in practice_controller.go (Submit ~line 91, Preview ~line 135) with a resolved category schema. Flow: GetPracticeQuestion already returns the question; extend it (ARCH-013) to also return category_id; controller resolves schema via repo (GetPracticeCategorySchema(categoryID) -> 'practice_cat_<id>', or join in GetPracticeQuestion to return SchemaName directly - preferred, one query). Pass that schema string as the sandboxSchema arg to validator.Validate / validator.ValidatePreview (signatures already accept sandboxSchema - no change needed). CRITICAL FIX for true separation: the QUERY (SELECT) evaluation path currently hardcodes 'SET LOCAL search_path TO public' (evaluateQuery postgres.go:1493, evaluateQueryPreview postgres.go:1611) and IGNORES sandboxSchema, so today practice SELECT reads the exam's public curriculum. For category separation, practice SELECT must read the CATEGORY schema. Because Evaluate/evaluateQuery do not currently receive sandboxSchema for the QUERY branch, the design adds the schema to the QUERY path: thread sandboxSchema into evaluateQuery/evaluateQueryPreview and change their 'SET LOCAL search_path TO public' to 'SET LOCAL search_path TO <sandboxSchema>, public' (keeping public as fallback for shared lookups), under exam_student_readonly. This is the single most important correctness change: without it, practice SELECT questions ignore their category's database entirely. DML path (evaluateDML postgres.go:1521) already consumes sandboxSchema with SAVEPOINT/ROLLBACK and needs no logic change beyond receiving the category schema. The savepoint-rollback semantics (user decision 4) are thus preserved unchanged for DML and the category schema state is never mutated. Capture (CreatePracticeQuestion's expected-result capture) must ALSO run against the category schema, not public (see ARCH-016b note inside): the practice question's correct_sql is captured at author time - that capture currently runs in public via WithTransaction; for category questions it must SET LOCAL search_path to the category schema so the expected result reflects the category's data. ResetSandbox endpoint (practice_controller.go:256, POST /lecturer/practice/reset-sandbox using ResetPracticeSandbox) becomes OBSOLETE for category practice: savepoint-rollback already restores per-submission state and there is no single shared sandbox to reset. Recommendation: retire the global reset-sandbox endpoint; if a per-category 'reset/reseed' is wanted it is equivalent to re-import (ARCH-014 replace mode, OQ-3). The legacy sandbox_practice schema + app.practice_sandbox_state + InitializePracticeSandbox (cmd/main.go:57) become dead once all questions are category-backed; plan their removal in ARCH-018.
arch_decisions.rationale: Decision 4 (user-locked): savepoint-and-rollback inside the category's own schema, no per-submission cloning. Investigation found the DML path already does exactly this and takes a schema arg, so DML just needs the right schema. The non-obvious, load-bearing discovery is that the QUERY/SELECT path hardcodes public and ignores the schema arg - leaving it unfixed would silently defeat the entire separation goal for SELECT questions. Capturing expected results in the category schema keeps practice validation self-consistent with the category's data. Retiring reset-sandbox follows directly from savepoint-rollback making a shared reset meaningless.

arch_decisions.decision: Schema-introspection repository capability: GetSchemaTablesWithColumns(ctx, schema string) -> []TableIntrospection. New repo method in backend/internal/repository/postgres.go that, given a schema name ('public' for exams or 'practice_cat_<id>' for a practice category), returns its tables each with their columns. The shape (new Go structs, placed in backend/internal/models/introspection.go): TableIntrospection{ Name string `json:"name"`; Columns []ColumnIntrospection `json:"columns"` } and ColumnIntrospection{ Name string `json:"name"`; DataType string `json:"data_type"`; Nullable bool `json:"nullable"`; IsPrimaryKey bool `json:"is_primary_key"`; IsForeignKey bool `json:"is_foreign_key"`; ReferencesTable string `json:"references_table,omitempty"`; ReferencesColumn string `json:"references_column,omitempty"` }. Implementation: one query against information_schema.columns (table_name, column_name, data_type, is_nullable, ordinal_position) filtered by table_schema=$1, ordered by table_name, ordinal_position; PK membership via a join to information_schema.table_constraints + key_column_usage where constraint_type='PRIMARY KEY'; FK membership + referenced table/column via information_schema.table_constraints + key_column_usage + constraint_column_usage where constraint_type='FOREIGN KEY'. Use $1-parameterized table_schema (never string-concatenate the schema) — information_schema.* is queried with the schema as a DATA value, so no Identifier sanitization is needed and there is no SQL-injection surface. Returns an empty (non-nil) slice when the schema has no tables (not an error). NO actual row data is read (scope decision 1).
arch_decisions.rationale: The brief's central new primitive: column-level introspection does not exist yet (only GetPublicTables lists names). information_schema is the portable, read-only, parameterizable source for column attributes + key membership and never touches user row data, satisfying scope decision 1 (schema + columns only, no rows). A single repo method serving both 'public' and 'practice_cat_<id>' keeps exam-intro and practice-intro on one code path. Reusing data_type from information_schema gives human-readable types ('integer', 'character varying') without pg_catalog OID decoding.

arch_decisions.decision: API surface: a quartet of endpoints per scope (practice category + examination) for listing metadata, streaming a single image's bytes, uploading a new image, deleting an image, and batch-updating sort order. PRACTICE category, registered in the practiceStudent group for reads (cmd/main.go:186-197, behind AuthMiddleware + RoleMiddleware(RoleStudent) + practiceFreezeMW) and in practiceLecturer for writes (cmd/main.go:200-215, behind AuthMiddleware + RoleMiddleware(Admin, Lecturer)): (1) GET /api/v1/practice/categories/:id/intro-images → []{id, sort_order, mime_type, byte_size, updated_at} ordered by sort_order ASC, id ASC; 404 if category missing; 200 with empty array if none. (2) GET /api/v1/practice/categories/:id/intro-images/:imageId → streams raw bytes with Content-Type: <mime_type>, Content-Length: <byte_size>, Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400, must-revalidate, ETag: "<updated_at unix epoch seconds>". Honors If-None-Match → 304 when the ETag matches. 404 if category or image missing, 404 if the imageId is not owned by :id (path consistency check). (3) POST /api/v1/practice/categories/:id/intro-images, Content-Type: multipart/form-data with field 'image' (single file). Server validates: file size <= 5 MB (else 413), aggregate scope size after upload <= 25 MB (else 413), detected mime via magic bytes (PNG signature 89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A or JPEG SOI/APP marker FF D8 FF) — DO NOT trust the multipart Content-Type header (else 415). sort_order is assigned server-side as MAX(sort_order)+1 in a single transaction (so the just-uploaded image lands last); 201 returns the new IntroImageMetadata row. 404 if category missing. (4) DELETE /api/v1/practice/categories/:id/intro-images/:imageId → 204; 404 if not found. No automatic sort_order compaction (gaps are fine; ORDER BY sort_order ASC still works). (5) PUT /api/v1/practice/categories/:id/intro-images/order with body {order: [{id, sort_order}, ...]} — batch update in a single transaction, validates that every supplied id belongs to :id (else 400 with the offending id) and that ids are not duplicated. 200. EXAMINATION quartet at /api/v1/quiz/exams/:id/intro-images and /api/v1/quiz/exams/:id/intro-images/:imageId (student reads — gated on IsStudentEnrolledInExam, same shape as ARCH-025: enrollment-gated NOT active-gated, since the intro is reachable at exam start and revisitable mid-exam), and lecturer writes at /api/v1/lecturer/exams/:id/intro-images (POST, DELETE, PUT order) in the staff group (cmd/main.go:158-181, RoleMiddleware(Admin, Lecturer)). All write endpoints update the parent row's updated_at-equivalent free-text introduction is NOT touched; only the image row's updated_at moves. AUTH for practice student GET: matches the practice intro precedent (ARCH-024) — passes practiceFreezeMW so during a focus-mode exam it returns 423 along with the rest of practice. AUTH for exam student GET: enrollment-gated only (matches ARCH-025); the intro is curriculum context and reveals no answers, so allowing it pre-activation is safe and required for the 'first page after start' flow. FILE upload size cap is enforced via Gin's c.Request.ContentLength check BEFORE buffering AND via a defensive http.MaxBytesReader wrapper (5 MB + small slack for the multipart envelope) to prevent the server from buffering a hostile 1 GB payload.
arch_decisions.rationale: Splitting metadata-list from byte-stream is the single most important shape decision: the list endpoint stays small and JSON-cacheable, and the browser fetches individual image bytes lazily via standard with normal HTTP caching. ETag = updated_at epoch is the cheapest correct cache key (no hashing needed) and 304s on revisit cost a single SELECT updated_at. Magic-byte detection is the only reliable mime check; trusting the multipart header would let a renamed .exe through. Server-assigned sort_order on upload (MAX+1) means lecturers never have to think about ordering during upload — they just upload and then reorder; this matches the row-shape semantics in PracticeAuthoring.vue where order is managed AFTER creation. Batch reorder via a single endpoint (not N PATCHes) prevents intermediate inconsistent states (sort_order collisions) and keeps the UI to one round-trip on save. Gating exam reads on enrollment-only (matching ARCH-025) keeps both intro components — text+tables in ARCH-025, images here — reachable on the same timeline (first page of active phase + revisitable mid-exam).

arch_decisions.decision: Storage / encoding strategy: store image bytes as raw PostgreSQL BYTEA, no compression wrapper, no base64, no filesystem. Per-image hard cap: 5 MB (enforced by ARCH-028 CHECK constraint + controller pre-buffer guard via http.MaxBytesReader). Per-scope soft cap: 25 MB aggregate (enforced by the upload controller via a SUM(byte_size) pre-flight check inside the same transaction as the INSERT; returns 413 with a friendly aggregate message). NO server-side downscale / re-encode in v1 — uploads are written as received (after magic-byte validation). Bytes are sent to the client uncompressed via Content-Type: image/png or image/jpeg; gzip Content-Encoding is NOT enabled for these responses because PNG and JPEG are already entropy-coded and gzipping them wastes CPU for ~0% ratio gain. Bytea is read from pgx as []byte (no streaming) — at 5 MB per image and a handful per scope this is comfortably below request-handler memory budgets and avoids the complexity of a pgx large-object lo_* API.
arch_decisions.rationale: PNG and JPEG payloads are already DEFLATE / Huffman-coded; gzip on top yields essentially no size reduction (typically <2%) and burns CPU on every fetch. Base64 inflates payload ~33% with no benefit since BYTEA already handles binary cleanly through pgx. Filesystem storage would introduce a new operational concern (volume mount, backup separation, dev/prod parity) for a tiny dataset (estimated total per deployment: a few dozen MB). DB storage is captured by existing pg_dump backups for free. Skipping server-side downscale in v1 keeps the architect's scope tight and removes a non-trivial dependency (Go image/* decode, transparency handling, EXIF orientation, JPEG quality tuning). The 5 MB cap is generous for schema diagrams (which are typically tens to hundreds of KB) and pushes the responsibility for reasonable sizing to the lecturer, with the documented option to add downscale later if real usage shows a problem. The 25 MB aggregate cap is a soft guardrail against accidental abuse, sized to allow ~5 large diagrams per scope while preventing a single category from ballooning to GB-scale via repeated re-uploads.

issues.issue: Broadcast copies the channel set under RLock then releases the lock before the non-blocking send. Unsubscribe removes ch from the map under write lock then close(ch) at line 45 AFTER releasing the lock. Race window: Broadcast snapshots ch -> Unsubscribe removes+closes ch -> Broadcast does `select { case ch <- payload }` on a CLOSED channel -> panic: send on closed channel. Confirmed with `go test -race`: data race + 'panic: send on closed channel' reproduced. This is live in production: a student disconnecting (StreamExamStatus defer Unsubscribe) concurrent with ActivateExamination/lazy-GetExamQuestions Broadcast for the same examID crashes the whole backend process.
issues.fix: Do not close the channel in Unsubscribe while a Broadcast may hold a reference. Options: (a) close(ch) INSIDE the write-locked critical section AND have Broadcast send under the read lock (accept holding RLock during non-blocking sends — sends are non-blocking so this is safe and cheap); or (b) never close subscriber channels — let Unsubscribe only delete from the map and rely on GC + the handler's ctx.Done() to stop the reader; or (c) guard each channel with a per-sub closed flag / recover() in Broadcast's send. Simplest correct fix: move the send loop in Broadcast under h.mu.RLock and close(ch) under h.mu.Lock in Unsubscribe (a writer cannot run while a reader holds RLock, so no send-on-closed).
